claims.text: In ATAM each analysed scenario's decisions are recorded as risks, non-risks, sensitivity points and trade-off points, one label per record row (one decision for the scenarios it names); the output is these findings, not an overall mark.
claims.source_hint: ATAM method description (technical report introducing ATAM): outputs of the analysis step; glossary atam, sensitivity-point, trade-off-point

claims.text: Findings table (lines 57-64): K1 catalog-reads = risk R1; K1 orders = risk R2; K1 PermitLimit of catalog-reads = sensitivity point; K2 data layout left by ADR 0012 = risk R3; K4 refund = non-risk; shared deployment (K1, K2, K3, K5) = trade-off point: helps K3, K5, makes K1, K2 harder.

catalog-reads is one limit on concurrent product reads for the whole api process, no per-customer or per-shop count: PermitLimit 20, QueueLimit 5 in code; a read beyond that is refused; one busy shop can fill it and other shops' reads get 503.

In ASP.NET Core rate limiting, a refused request does not reach the endpoint; the middleware's default RejectionStatusCode is 503, and Đơn Hàng's OnRejected changes it to 429 only when the lease has RetryAfter metadata, which a concurrency limiter does not give.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Rate limiting middleware (RejectionStatusCode, OnRejected, ConcurrencyLimiter); Program.cs @ stage-4 lines 168-181

claims.text: The orders policy partitions by the access token's sub claim (GetFixedWindowLimiter keyed by customer), nothing in it refers to the shop; signed-out callers get no limiter; ordersLimit (Program.cs line 140) is 10 per 1-minute window.

ADR 0012 serves every shop from one shared deployment and leaves each shop's data layout to a later ADR (R3); the review records isolation between shops as risk R3 and hands the question on without deciding it.

Refunds (K4) are a non-risk: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/refund saves request and message in one transaction and answers 202 without calling the payment gateway, whichever shop sends it; K4 is written from YC-7, which holds as for one shop.

Risk themes (lines 66-71): R1 and R2 grouped as limits that know no shop, because both point at one decision to revisit (load limits must know the request's shop); R3, data isolation not decided, is a second theme.

Next steps (lines 73-78): R1, R2 owned by the team lead: propose an ADR on per-shop limits and, when built, add a fitness function; R3 owned by a backend developer: propose the data layout ADR with a check that one shop cannot read another's data.

Record lines 80-81 (after the findings excerpt): Program.cs keeps catalog-reads and orders unchanged until the ADR for R1, R2 is built. The last section records R3 taken up by ADR 0013 and R1, R2 by ADR 0016.
ADR 0012's consequences say the existing limits (orders, catalog-reads in Program.cs) do not know the shop.
The sensitivity point row (line 61): PermitLimit too low and every shop gets 503 early; too high and the shared database takes the whole load. Raising the limit leaves it shared, so R1 remains.
The review did not reopen ADR 0012 although it found R1-R3: re-deciding it was out of scope (line 19); the trade-off row (line 64) records that the shared deployment makes K3 and K5 easy.
A review should end in risks tied to decisions, grouped into themes, each with an owner and next step, rather than a verdict, a bare list or fixes made in the session (trade-offs table).

Choices: a risk inside one module with one sensible fix can take a pull request as next step; to answer the product owner, say which risks must be answered before building (R3 first); a risk whose decision belongs to another team goes to an owner in that team.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 6; ADR 0012 revisit conditions (team growth)

claims.text: Misconceptions: a review is not pass or fail; finding risks does not make the decision wrong; risks are not fixed in the same session.

Scenarios (record lines 34-38, 42-43): K1 other shops keep usual product-read errors and order response times during one shop's sale; K2 no row of another shop; K4 refund answered within 2 s when the gateway fails; K3, K5 (open shop, change settings, no deploy) not analysed.
